Text: {D(HouseMember)} found a chest of old family heirlooms

It’s mostly old documents and letters, but a coin embossed with a name and coordinates within {StarSystem} catches your attention. They point to a large asteroid. Strange, you think. There are no records of a colony ever being established there. Orbitting the asteroid, your scanners detect a structure on the surface. As the complex rises up below you, {d(HouseMember)} gasps: “It’s a prison!” “It was,” you correct {him(HouseMember)}. No lights, no guards, no prisoners. You step through a hole blown through the entrance building. “We should hurry. This place reeks of violence” says {d(HouseMember)}.
Scouring the prison records, you match the name on the coin

Sentenced for life. “Given the condition of this place, it’s likely that ended prematurely... one way or another,” you mutter. You open the box with the prisoner’s belongings. Dust. Old military pins. A photograph.

“Hold on”, says {d(HouseMember)}, “isn’t this an old member of {EnemyHouse}?” You take a look. Sentenced for life. Treason. “This will make for an interesting conversation with {EnemyDuke},” you say, copying the record with your pad.
{EnemyDuke} is the direct descendant of an escaped prisoner
It was revealed that {Character} is the direct descendant of an escaped prisoner
Found out {EnemyDuke} is the direct descendant of an escaped prisoner
A noise echoes through the building

“Hello?” you shout. No answer.

“We really ought to leave,” says {d(HouseMember)}.
As you leave, you hear frantic shouting; bullets whiz past you
You sprint to the ship and fall into your seats. {D(HouseMember)} lets out a slow whistle. "That was close. What should be done about this place?"
We no longer concern ourselves with it
Seize it, it will prove valuable in the long run
After a tough battle, {d(PlayerCharacter)} seized the prison asteroid
You follow the signs to the medcenter

Suddenly, you hear faint voices. You raise your gun and sneak down the corridor. Is that music? Children? Everything goes quiet as you walk through the door. Beds, belongings, women and children all crammed together. “We’re not here to hurt anybody,” you say. “But who the hell are you?” The musician, an old lady with a bionic arm, replies. “We’re what’s left of this place. After the uprising, it became our home.” She nods to a group of mothers and their children. “Most never knew this place back in its heyday. Word of advice: we’re no threat to you. But when the others return with food and plunder, that little gun of yours won’t help much.”
You turn to leave when a shape leaps from a hole in the ceiling

With catlike movement, it lands on the ground and looks up. It’s a boy, barely of age.

“Where the hell did you come from?” you cry.

“I know every nook and cranny of this place,” the boy replies without hesitation. "In fact, I can get in and out of any building I please.”

“Great. We’re leaving.”

“Wait!” the boy pleads. “Take me with you! I don’t want to live here anymore. I promise, I’ll be useful!”

“I don’t know why I expected anything else,” you say, taking in the ravaged armoury. You inspect the large safe at the far end. The doors were blown off. You notice scratches on the ground.

“Help me push this,” you say to {d(HouseMember)}. Together, you manage to move the safe, revealing a hole in the wall. Behind it, stolen trinkets. You recognize some of them as being stolen from {StarSystem}. As its acting Duke, you confiscate them all.

“Give me one good reason not to kill you,” a cold voice says behind you

You turn around and face a small gang of bandits. 
"Because I’m the Head of {House} and killing me will mean the end of you all,” you reply slowly.

A bald brute with a gun in one hand and a sabre in the other starts laughing.
“We know who you are; just wanted to test you,” he says, his smile revealing several diamond teeth.

“Leave now and never return. There’s nothing of value for you here; only pain. Do we have a mutual agreement?”

You nod.
